name: AGC 731921 (Hubble)
blurb: AGC 731921, a gas-rich dwarf galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: agc731921-hubble
story: A small, gas-rich dwarf galaxy first picked out by the ALFALFA survey, a radio survey that mapped neutral hydrogen gas across the sky. Hubble resolved its individual stars so astronomers could measure how far away it lies.

claims.text: AGC 731921 is one of the low-mass dwarf galaxies targeted by HST program 13750 (SHIELD II), at the observed position
AGC 731921 is a gas-rich dwarf galaxy in the SHIELD sample
SHIELD galaxies were selected from the ALFALFA survey (Arecibo), which mapped neutral hydrogen across the sky
Hubble images of resolved stars were used to measure the distances of these galaxies
